archetype.name: Playoff Team (guard-led, glass-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose top-ten ratings on both ends come from an elite backcourt and one of the league's best rebounding units, good enough to make the playoffs comfortably but not yet a team that has beaten good opponents.

report.headline: A real jump from 25 wins, but the 6-0 start oversold it
report.take:
Memphis is the league's most interesting turnaround so far. Last season's 25-57 team had a 118.8 defensive rating. This one is at 110, eighth in the league, with a 116.1 offense (10th) on top of it, for a Net Rtg of 6.1 that also ranks eighth. The record isn't a mirage built on close games. W vs Pt Diff sits at 0, the margin implies exactly the six wins they have, and the full-season pace reads 55 wins. The site has them eighth of 30. That is a playoff profile on paper, nine games in.

Two things drive it. The first is the backcourt, graded A. Ty Jerome is the engine, using 32.1% of possessions on 62.9 TS % with a 7.1 BPM and the team 10.4 points better with him on the floor. Cedric Coward (5th on the SG tab, +20.5 On-Off) and Cam Spencer (68.2 TS %, 6.1 BPM) give it real depth. The second is the glass. Memphis is first in RPG at 48.8, second in REB % and third in DRB %, and that ends opposing possessions after one shot. Add a 3P % of 37.8, fifth and well above the league's 34.7, and an opponent rim rate (26.2) among the league's lowest, and you get efficient shots for and few easy ones against.

What the numbers hide is the shape of the season. All six wins came in October, the last six of them away from home or against Utah and Sacramento twice each. November opened with three straight losses at home: an overtime loss to New Orleans, a loss to Indiana and a 97-128 drubbing by Oklahoma City. Over the last five they allowed 3.82 more points a game than their season mark. The forward spots are a problem too. The wings are graded D and barely play. Kris Murray is shooting 28.3 TS %. The most-used player on the roster, Cameron Boozer, is at 49.4 TS % with a -11.5 On-Off. Jerami Grant (-9.6) and GG Jackson II (-15.1) also post negative lineup numbers. Isaiah Stewart, scoring at 78.5 TS % with a +8.1 On-Off, is listed Out.

The direction is still clearly up from last year. History supports the rebounding identity: the 2021-22 team that won 56 had the same 53.3 REB %. Expect the three-point shooting to cool and the net rating to settle somewhere below its current level. The guards and the glass should hold, which points to a solid playoff team rather than the 55-win juggernaut the pace suggests.

strengths.title: An A-grade, deep backcourt
strengths.body: Jerome, Coward and Spencer all post strong impact numbers. Jerome is 8th on the PG tab with a 7.1 BPM, and Coward has the team's best On-Off. The group's quality is spread across three players, not carried by one, so it should survive a cold stretch from any single guard. Jerome's 32.1 USG % is heavy, but he is converting it efficiently.

strengths.title: Dominant on the glass
strengths.body: Memphis is first in RPG and second in REB %, and its DRB % of 76.2 is far above the league's 72.4. That ends opposing possessions and underpins the top-ten defense. It is a big swing from last season's 47.4 REB %, but it matches the franchise's 2021-22 profile, and rebounding tends to be one of the stickier team traits.

strengths.title: A rebuilt defense that walls off the rim
strengths.body: The defensive rating has dropped from 118.8 last season to 110, eighth in the league. Opponents are taking only 26.2% of their shots at the rim, sixth-lowest. Opponents finish at the rim at a middling rate (Opp Rim FG % ranks 18th), so the defense works by keeping shots out of the paint rather than by blocking them there. Stewart's absence tests that.

concerns.title: Forward spots are a hole
concerns.body: The wings grade D and the frontcourt D+. Murray's 28.3 TS % and Boozer's 49.4 TS % on heavy usage drag the offense. Boozer, Grant and Jackson all post negative On-Off numbers, so the lineups get worse when the forwards play big minutes. Unless Boozer's efficiency rises, the team leans on its guards to cover for him.

concerns.title: The October run may have flattered
concerns.body: The 6-0 October was followed by an 0-3 start to November, including a 97-128 loss to Oklahoma City. The defense has slipped over the last five games. The sheet doesn't rate those October opponents, so how much of the start was schedule is an open question. The first tougher tests went badly.

concerns.title: Hot shooting, Stewart out
concerns.body: A 3P % 3.1 points above the league average is the kind of edge that usually narrows. Memphis also rarely gets to the line (FT Rate ranks 24th), so the offense has little to lean on when the threes stop falling. Stewart, its most efficient big, is listed Out.

trend.note: An unbeaten October gave way to three straight November losses. The point differential is still positive over the last five, but the defense has leaked more points lately.

weekAhead.headline: Three sub-.500 opponents and a glass edge: a week to reset
weekAhead.body:
Five games in eight days, three of them on the road, with a back-to-back at New Orleans and home to Brooklyn. Only Toronto (5-4) and Denver (5-3) have winning records. Neither sits higher than 16th on the site, and Memphis has the better Net Rtg than all five opponents. Brooklyn's offense ranks 28th and Washington's 23rd. Washington is 29th in REB %, the kind of team Memphis's rebounding should punish.

The danger games are the first two and the rematch with New Orleans, which beat them in overtime. Toronto forces turnovers better than anyone, against a Memphis offense that ranks only 18th in TOV %. Denver's offense ranks 7th. Coming off three losses, anything less than a winning week would deepen the doubts about the start.

keyMatchups.title: Ball security against Toronto
keyMatchups.body: Toronto leads the league in Opp TOV %, and Memphis gives the ball away at a below-average rate. Toronto also leads the league in ORB %, so the Grizzlies' defensive glass gets its stiffest test of the week. On the other side, Toronto allows the most points in the league to shooting guards, which favors Coward, Wells and Spencer.

keyMatchups.title: Denver squeezes guards, opens forwards
keyMatchups.body: Denver has allowed the fewest points to shooting guards but ranks near the bottom against power forwards. That is a chance for Boozer to find a rhythm against a defense ranked 19th. Memphis's SG depth may be muted that night.

keyMatchups.title: Jerome against the Pelicans' perimeter
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans allows a lot of points to point guards, ranking 27th, and its defense ranks 21st overall. Jerome should get his shots in the rematch. The Pelicans' A+ frontcourt is a real test with Stewart out.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the defense that leaked points over the last five tightens against weaker offenses like Brooklyn and Washington, or whether November's slide is the real level.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation looks real: an efficient, deep backcourt and a rebounding edge that this franchise has shown before. The 55-win pace is the ceiling, not the forecast. The 37.8 3P % should cool, and the three November losses suggest the October margin was partly the opponents. The forward rotation is also costing them on both ends. Settling into a net rating in the low-to-mid single digits points to a final total in the 44-51 win range. That would be a playoff seed and a dramatic jump from 25 wins.

The upside case runs through the frontcourt. If Boozer's efficiency climbs from 49.4 TS % and Stewart returns, the weakest groups become average, and the guards and glass can carry Memphis toward the top of the West's middle class. The downside is an offense that leans on threes, rarely gets to the line and turns it over a bit too often. In a cold-shooting month, that could slide them toward the play-in.

confidence.note: Nine games, a split between an unbeaten October and a winless November, and a key big out.
